verbalization: Trans-urocanic acid appears to interact with the Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2 through a series of molecular pathways. The evidence suggests that trans-urocanic acid acts as a substrate for Isopentenyl-diphosphate Delta-isomerase, an enzyme that catalyzes the isomerization of isopentenyl-diphosphate. This enzyme is subsequently targeted by a specific compound, which in turn targets the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2. This implies a potential regulatory mechanism where trans-urocanic acid influences the activity of the enzyme, which in turn affects the function of the G protein subunit. The observed scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the interaction may be biologically relevant. However, further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of trans-urocanic acid in the regulation of the G protein subunit gamma-2.
